newsitem.title: USA: Sears sees mid-teens annual EPS over 5 years.
newsitem.headline: Sears sees mid-teens annual EPS over 5 years.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co chairman and chief executive Arthur Martinez on Wednesday reiterated the retailer's goal of an earnings per share growth rate in the mid-teens for the next five years.
"We have a high confidence in our ability to do this," Martinez told analysts here, referring to that goal.
Chief Financial Officer Alan Lacy said he is comfortable the company will meet that target in 1997.
"At this stage of the year, to say we are comfortable with that is appropriate," Lacy said in response to a question.
During his presentation to analysts, Lacy said same store sales should grow in the mid-single digits.

"We expect to continue to see mid-single digit comparable store sales increases," Lacy said, adding that total sales from the company are expected to be four to five percent higher than that due to new stores.
Sears reported 1996 revenues from domestic operations rose 10.2 percent from a year earlier to $34.85 billion.

Lacy also said a change in accounting standards regarding credit operations should add $100 million to $150 million to net income in 1997 and $50 million to $75 million in 1998. He added that the retailer sees this as a non-recurring event that should not be factored into analysts earnings estimates.
